---
title: "What practitioners told us about AI at ACLCA 2026"
date: 2026-09-15
description: "Survey and breakout results from our special session, and what they mean for our guidance."
categories: [Events, AI for LCA, Design flexibility]
---

Our 90-minute special session at ACLCA 2026 drew roughly 80 people. About 40 answered a live survey on using AI for LCA of emerging technologies, followed by two rounds of breakout discussions.

## Where AI sits in practice today

Literature review (33 respondents) and data gathering (28) lead, followed by writing code (17), running the LCA steps (11), and building the process model itself (9). The closer a task is to the core model, the less people use AI.

## What people want from guidance

Asked what our guidance would need to contain for them to use it, respondents split almost evenly: worked examples (29), disclosure templates (26), and a decision tool by TRL (25). Our first drafts of all three are on the [guidance pages](../guidance/index.qmd).

## Themes from the discussions

1. **Assist, do not invent.** Using AI to generate data that does not exist was described as bordering on malpractice.
2. **Trust but verify, at every TRL.** Several people named thresholds, such as below pilot scale, where verification becomes essential, because bench scale data does not always scale.
3. **Keep judgment human.** Goal and scope, boundaries, allocation, and interpretation should stay with the practitioner.
4. **Disclose.** A strong majority favored disclosing which numbers and content were AI assisted.
5. **Is 90 percent enough?** The best answers asked first whether the missing 10 percent matters for the decision. For a screening study, it may not.

## Design flexibility breakout

The second breakout asked when design choices lock in. Answers ranged from before TRL 4 for siting a biomass pyrolysis plant to TRL 7 to 8 for a bio-based manufacturing process. See the [design flexibility project](../projects/design-flexibility.qmd).

Thank you to everyone who took part.
